actions.action: Reserve one worker for customer fairness.
actions.mechanism: Round-robin customer turns bound dispatch delay independently of file-size estimates; this is not a mean-latency guarantee.
actions.implementation: Dedicate one of twelve workers to oldest-job customer round-robin. Append newly active customers behind waiting turns; remove empty customers.
actions.check: A waiting customer with N−1 turns ahead starts within 60N seconds, excluding scheduler overhead. Verify from dispatch logs.
actions.risk: Reserving capacity can reduce utilization when only long jobs remain.

actions.mechanism: Estimated-shortest selection favors small jobs; recurring oldest-job selections protect underestimated and large jobs from indefinite bypass.
actions.implementation: On the other eleven workers, use estimated-shortest selection for three dispatches, then select the globally oldest queued job. Coordinate dequeues atomically.
actions.check: Under mixed arrivals, compare short-job start delay with FIFO; verify every fourth dispatch selects the oldest available job.
actions.risk: Misestimated long jobs still occupy workers for up to sixty seconds.

actions.mechanism: Adversarial replay exposes estimate errors and sustained-load starvation that aggregate latency can conceal.
actions.implementation: Continuously replenish one customer's sixty-second jobs; inject other customers' one-second jobs and long jobs. Reverse estimates, then repeat with accurate estimates.
actions.check: Verify the fairness bound and oldest-job dispatch rule; report per-customer starts, short-job latency, and overall mean latency separately.
actions.risk: An overloaded queue can grow indefinitely despite guaranteed customer progress.
